scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF
from each other!! From the department head's machine (it_hod) none of the CS
computers (the 192.168.2.x ones) answer any more -- our own department is
fine, it's just CS that's gone. The router that joins the two departments has
obviously dropped one of its sides -- it's still talking to us but it has let
go of CS, one hundred percent!! Please plug the CS side back into the router
and rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce any outage between the IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) departments. The inter-VLAN routing component (router0) appears healthy.

Mechanism/evidence:
- From it_hod (192.168.1.2) I can reach multiple CS hosts with 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT: cs_hod (192.168.2.2), cs_lab1 (.3), cs_lab2 (.4), cs_lab3 (.5), cs_lab4 (.6).
- Reverse direction also works: cs_hod → it_hod succeeds with 0% loss.
- Router0 has both departmental interfaces up and carrying traffic: eth0 192.168.1.1/24 and eth1 192.168.2.1/24 show UP/LOWER_UP with connected routes present for 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24.
- The L2 access switches on both sides (switch0 for IT, switch1 for CS) have their bridged ports up.

Localization:
- No failing interface or daemon found. router0 eth0 and eth1 are operational; CS and IT hosts have correct default gateways; traffic passes in both directions.

Root cause:
No current fault found; the reported symptom is not present at this time (likely transient or a mistaken observation).

Corrective fix:
No changes required. Recommend closing the ticket as “not reproduced.” If the issue recurs intermittently, enable brief monitoring on router0 interfaces eth0/eth1 and switch1 to capture link flaps or errors and review logs/ARP tables at the time of impact.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router0's IT and CS interfaces are UP/LOWER_UP with connected routes and demonstrates successful IT↔CS connectivity, confirming baseline inter-department routing is healthy.

Overall the evidence and inferences logically support a 'not reproducible' diagnosis.
